state.seed_assertion: Processing where you obtain data from third parties requires that you must first carefully consider whether you can provide privacy information to the individuals.

sentences.1: Processing where you obtain data from third parties requires that you must first carefully consider whether you can provide privacy information to the individuals.
sentences.2: So, if you are proposing processing operations that involve the use of data obtained from third parties, you must first carefully consider whether you can provide privacy information to the individuals.
sentences.3: Invisible processing occurs when you obtain personal data from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and you do not provide them with the privacy information required by Article 14.
sentences.4: 'Invisible processing' occurs when you obtain personal data from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and you don't provide them with the privacy information required by Article 14.
sentences.5: Matching and/or combining personal data originating from multiple sources or third parties, or for two or more data processing operations performed for different purposes and/or by different data controllers in a way that would exceed the reasonable expectations of the data subjects is a type of processing subject to DPIA requirement.
sentences.6: Matching and/or combining personal data originating from multiple sources or third parties, or for two or more data processing operations performed for different purposes and/or by different data controllers in a way that would exceed the reasonable expectations of the data subjects.
sentences.7: If the processing is wholly or partly performed by a data processor, the processor should assist the controller in carrying out the DPIA and provide any necessary information in line with Article 28(3)(f).
sentences.8: If the processing is wholly or partly performed by a data processor, the processor should assist the controller in carrying out the DPIA and provide any necessary information (in line with Article 28(3)(f)).
sentences.9: 'Invisible processing' occurs when you obtain personal data from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and you don't provide them with the privacy information required by Article 14.
sentences.10: These include where to provide the privacy information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort.
sentences.11: Invisible processing occurs when personal data is obtained from somewhere other than directly from the individual themselves, and privacy information required by Article 14 is not provided.
sentences.12: Invisible processing is only permitted by the UK GDPR in limited circumstances, such as where providing privacy information proves impossible or would involve disproportionate effort.
